Nutrient-drug interactions
The standard treatment for all newly diagnosed patients with active, drug-susceptible TB includes four drugs, isoniazid, rifampin,
pyrazinamide, and ethambutol, taken for two to three months followed by two of these drugs, isoniazid and rifampicin, taken for
an additional four to 6 months. Isoniazid (INH) interferes with the metabolism of vitamin B6 which includes pyridoxine, pyridoxal,
and pyridoxamine. Isoniazid combines with pyridoxal or pyridoxal phosphate to form potent inhibitors of pyridoxal kinase, thus,
blocking formation of the coenzyme form of the vitamin. In the absence of vitamin B6 supplements, TB patients treated with INH
may experience peripheral neuritis, manifested as tingling, numbness, or a painful “prickly” sensation in a stocking and glove distri-
bution. Approximately 20% of patients treated with high doses of INH or patients who are otherwise predisposed to peripheral
